arxiv-2201-02067.title: Uncertainty Quantification Techniques for Space Weather Modeling: Thermospheric Density Application
arxiv-2201-02067.creator: Richard J. Licata, Piyush M. Mehta
arxiv-2201-02067.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Richard J. Licata, Piyush M. Mehta. Machine learning (ML) has been applied to space weather problems with increasing frequency in recent years, driven by an influx of in-situ measurements and a desire to improve modeling and forecasting capabilities throughout the field. Space weather originates from solar perturbations and is comprised of the resulting complex variations they cause within the numerous systems between the Sun and Earth. These systems are often tightly coupled and not well understood.

arxiv-2201-09141.title: Chains of path geometries on surfaces: theory and examples
arxiv-2201-09141.creator: Gil Bor, Travis Willse
arxiv-2201-09141.description: Abstract We derive the equations of chains for path geometries on surfaces by solving the equivalence problem of a related structure: sub-Riemannian geometry of signature ( 1 , 1 ) (1,1) on a contact 3-manifold. This approach is significantly simpler than the standard method of solving the full equivalence problem for path geometry.

arxiv-2206-04790.title: Learn2Augment: Learning to Composite Videos for Data Augmentation in Action Recognition
arxiv-2206-04790.creator: Shreyank N Gowda, Marcus Rohrbach, Frank Keller, Laura Sevilla-Lara
arxiv-2206-04790.description: Abstract We address the problem of data augmentation for video action recognition. Standard augmentation strategies in video are hand-designed and sample the space of possible augmented data points either at random, without knowing which augmented points will be better, or through heuristics.

arxiv-2212-06733.title: Profit and loss decomposition in continuous time and approximations
arxiv-2212-06733.creator: Gero Junike, Hauke Stier, Marcus Christiansen
arxiv-2212-06733.description: Abstract Financial institutions and insurance companies that analyze the evolution and sources of profits and losses often look at risk factors only at discrete reporting dates, ignoring the detailed paths. Continuous-time decompositions avoid this weakness and also make decompositions consistent across different reporting grids.

arxiv-2212-11715.title: GeoCode: Interpretable Shape Programs
arxiv-2212-11715.creator: Ofek Pearl 1,2 Itai Lang 2 Yuhua Hu 2 Raymond A. Yeh 3 Rana Hanocka 2 1 Tel Aviv University 2 University of Chicago 3 Purdue University ofekpearl@mail.tau.ac.il {itailang, katehu, ranahanocka}@uchicago.edu rayyeh@purdue.edu, O. Pearl 1,2 I. Lang 2 Y. Hu 2 R. A. Yeh 3 R. Hanocka 2 1 Tel Aviv Universi
arxiv-2212-11715.description: Abstract The task of crafting procedural programs capable of generating structurally valid 3D shapes easily and intuitively remains an elusive goal in computer vision and graphics. Within the graphics community, generating procedural 3D models has shifted to using node graph systems. They allow the artist to create complex shapes and animations through visual programming.

arxiv-2307-01825.title: Self-similar solution for fractional Laplacian in cones Thanks: Krzysztof Bogdan was partially supported by the National Science Centre (Poland): grant 2017/27/B/ST1/01339. Łukasz Leżaj was partially supported by the National Science Centre (Poland): grant 2021/41/N/ST1/04139.
arxiv-2307-01825.creator: Krzysztof Bogdan 1,∗ , Piotr Knosalla 2 , Łukasz Leżaj 1,3,† and Dominika Pilarczyk 1,‡
arxiv-2307-01825.description: Abstract . We construct a self-similar solution of the heat equation for the fractional Laplacian with Dirichlet boundary conditions in every fat cone. Furthermore, we give the entrance law from the vertex and the Yaglom limit for the corresponding killed isotropic stable Lévy process and precise large-time asymptotics for solutions of the Cauchy problem in the cone.

arxiv-2311-10552.title: Analysis of Quantum Steering Measures
arxiv-2311-10552.creator: Lucas Maquedano ID, Ana C. S. Costa ID
arxiv-2311-10552.description: Abstract The effect of quantum steering describes a possible action at a distance via local measurements. In the last few years, several criteria have been proposed to detect this type of correlation in quantum systems. However, there are few approaches presented in order to measure the degree of steerability of a given system.

arxiv-2406-05175.title: Robust Quantum Dots Charge Autotuning using Neural Network Uncertainty
arxiv-2406-05175.creator: Victor Yon, Bastien Galaup, Claude Rohrbacher, Joffrey Rivard, Clément Godfrin, Ruoyu Li, Stefan Kubicek, Kristiaan De Greve, Louis Gaudreau, Eva Dupont-Ferrier, Yann Beilliard, Roger G. Melko, Dominique Drouin
arxiv-2406-05175.description: Abstract This study presents a machine learning-based procedure to automate the charge tuning of semiconductor spin qubits with minimal human intervention, addressing one of the significant challenges in scaling up quantum dot technologies. This method exploits artificial neural networks to identify noisy transition lines in stability diagrams, guiding a robust exploration strategy leveraging neural network uncertainty estimations.

arxiv-2407-19535.title: The Traveling Mailman: Topological Optimization Methods for User-Centric Redistricting
arxiv-2407-19535.creator: Nelson Colón Vargas
arxiv-2407-19535.description: Abstract This study introduces a new districting approach using the US Postal Service network to measure community connectivity. We combine Topological Data Analysis with Markov Chain Monte Carlo methods to assess district boundaries’ impact on community integrity. Using Iowa as a case study, we generate and refine districting plans using KMeans clustering and stochastic rebalancing.

arxiv-2408-07724.title: “Normalized Stress" is Not Normalized: How to Interpret Stress Correctly
arxiv-2408-07724.creator: Kiran Smelser, Jacob Miller, Stephen Kobourov
arxiv-2408-07724.description: Abstract Stress is among the most commonly employed quality metrics and optimization criteria for dimension reduction projections of high-dimensional data. Complex, high-dimensional data is ubiquitous across many scientific disciplines, including machine learning, biology, and the social sciences. One of the primary methods of visualizing these datasets is with two-dimensional scatter plots that visually capture some properties of the data.

arxiv-2412-10268.title: Almost Classical Skew Bracoids
arxiv-2412-10268.creator: Isabel Martin-Lyons
arxiv-2412-10268.description: Abstract . We investigate two sub-classes of skew bracoids, the first consists of those we term almost a brace , meaning the multiplicative group decomposes as a certain semi-direct product, and then those that are almost classical , which additionally specifies the relationship between the multiplicative group and the additive.

arxiv-2505-20604.title: Least Squares Model Reduction: A Two-Stage System-Theoretic Interpretation
arxiv-2505-20604.creator: Alberto Padoan
arxiv-2505-20604.description: Abstract Model reduction simplifies complex dynamical systems while preserving essential properties. This paper revisits a recently proposed system-theoretic framework for least squares moment matching. It interprets least squares model reduction in terms of two steps process: constructing a surrogate model to satisfy interpolation constraints, then projecting it onto a reduced-order space.

arxiv-2511-04003.title: A Generalized Frankel Conjecture Via The Yang-Mills Flow
arxiv-2511-04003.creator: Jiangtao Li
arxiv-2511-04003.description: Abstract . In this note, we introduce a new curvature condition called the 2 − 2- positive bisectional curvature on compact Kähler manifolds. We then deduce a characterization theorem for manifolds with 2 − 2- positive bisectional curvature, which can be regarded as a variant of the classical Frankel conjecture (cf.

arxiv-2605-18716.title: Recoupled Dark Radiation reconciling CMB and DESI BAO measurements Preprint: TTK-26-15
arxiv-2605-18716.creator: Ravi Kumar Sharma, Maria Archidiacono, Julien Lesgourgues

pmc-10606260.title: Statistical Mechanics Metrics in Pairing and Parsing In Silico and Phenotypic Data of a Novel Genetic NFκB1 (c.T638A) Variant
pmc-10606260.creator: Eman N Chaudhri, Jessica M Abbott, Naeyma N Islam, Caleb A Weber, Mathew A Coban, Ahmet Bilgili, Jacqueline D Squire, Sarah Mantia, Klaas J Wierenga, Thomas R Caulfield, Mitesh Dwivedi, Malgorzata Wasniewska
pmc-10606260.description: (1) Background: Mutations in NFκB1, a transcriptional regulator of immunomodulating proteins, are a known cause of inborn errors of immunity. Our proband is a 22-year-old male with a diagnosis of common variable immunodeficiency (CVID), cytopenias with massive splenomegaly, and nodular regenerative hyperplasia of the liver. Genetic studies identified a novel, single-point mutation variant in NFκB1, c. T638A p. V213E.

pmc-10628930.title: Chimeric antigen receptors in the brain: Can we tackle glioblastoma with engineered NK cells?
pmc-10628930.creator: Patrick Roth
pmc-10628930.description: onstrated only limited activity or was associated with toxicity.1 More recently, engineering patient-derived immune cells has become a game changer for hematological neoplasms such as lymphomas or multiple myeloma. Here, T cells that express a chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) have shown powerful antitumor activity, resulting in clinical approval. The situation is more challenging for solid tumors including glioblastoma.

pmc-10663896.title: Coronary sinus diameter to estimate congestion and predict survival
pmc-10663896.creator: Agatella Barchitta, Giacomo Rossitto, Luisa Ruzza, Daniele Maio, Giuseppe Scaparotta, Domenico Bagordo, Francesco Antonini Canterin, Piergiuseppe Piovesana, Teresa Maria Seccia, Federico Nalesso, Lorenzo Calò, Gian Paolo Rossi
pmc-10663896.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). BackgroundCongestion predicts a poor prognosis, but its assessment is challenging in clinical practice and requires a multiparametric approach. We investigated if the coronary sinus (CS) diameter can predict mortality in a human model of rapid fluid unloading.MethodsWe measured by echocardiography the CS, and the inferior vena cava (IVC) for comparison, in 60 patients with end-stage chronic kidney disease (ESKD) immediately before and after hemodialysis (HD; age 76 [57–81] years, 40% female, left ventricular ejection fraction 57 [53–56]%).

pmc-10735661.title: INTERGENERATIONAL BONDING: A PATHWAY TO CAREER READINESS IN SPEECH LANGUAGE PATHOLOGY GRADUATE STUDENTS
pmc-10735661.creator: Ladan Ghazi-Saidi, Miechelle McKelvey
pmc-10735661.description: We present a new experiential learning activity for graduate students in two core courses in Speech-Language Pathology. Speech-Language Pathology is a healthcare profession that provides care to people of all ages, including older adults with language, communication, and cognitive disorders. Students typically find these course contents heavy and have limited opportunity to practice the required skills for their future profession.

pmc-11304945.title: APIS: an updated parentage assignment software managing triploids induced from diploid parents
pmc-11304945.creator: Julien Roche, Ronan Griot, François Allal, Mathieu Besson, Pierrick Haffray, Pierre Patrice, Florence Phocas, Marc Vandeputte
pmc-11304945.description: In aquaculture, sterile triploids are commonly used for production as sterility gives them potential gains in growth, yields, and quality. However, they cannot be reproduced, and DNA parentage assignment to their diploid or tetraploid parents is required to estimate breeding values for triploid phenotypes. No publicly available software has the ability to assign triploids to their parents.

pmc-11509593.title: Genome-Wide Identification of the Remorin Gene Family in Poplar and Their Responses to Abiotic Stresses
pmc-11509593.creator: Zihui Li, Hang Wang, Chuanqi Li, Huimin Liu, Jie Luo, Balazs Barna
pmc-11509593.description: The Remorin (REM) gene family is a plant-specific, oligomeric, filamentous family protein located on the cell membrane, which is important for plant growth and stress responses. In this study, a total of 22 PtREMs were identified in the genome of Populus trichocarpa. Subcellular localization analysis showed that they were predictively distributed in the cell membrane and nucleus.

pmc-11550032.title: Harmonizing the complexities of financial development and fiscal decentralization in highly populated nations for monitoring environmental quality
pmc-11550032.creator: Yi Ding, Fayaz Hussain Tunio, Agha Amad Nabi
pmc-11550032.description: The increasing challenges posed by global warming underscore the need to examine the contributing factors comprehensively. This study explores the complex interaction that enhances the financial autonomy of local governments (fiscal decentralization), the evolution of financial development, and the dynamics of the environment in China, India, and Pakistan, which are known as highly populated economies.

pmc-11618349.title: Clustering explanation based on multi-hyperrectangle
pmc-11618349.creator: Tao Zeng, Caiming Zhong, Tiejun Pan
pmc-11618349.description: Clustering plays a crucial role in data mining and pattern recognition, but the interpretation of clustering results is often challenging. Existing interpretation methods usually lack an intuitive and accurate description of irregular shapes and high dimensional datas. This paper proposes a novel clustering explanation method based on a Multi-HyperRectangle(MHR), for extracting post hoc explanations of clustering results.

pmc-11651908.title: Identification and field testing of sex-attractant semiochemicals produced by male deer mice, Peromyscus maniculatus
pmc-11651908.creator: Elana Varner, Regine Gries, Stephen Takács, Hanna Jackson, Leah Purdey, Daniella Gofredo, Alishba Bibal, Gerhard Gries
pmc-11651908.description: Following previous reports that male deer mice, Peromyscus maniculatus, produce chemical signals that attract conspecific females, we analysed and field-tested sex-attractant semiochemicals (message-bearing chemicals) of male deer mice. Field traps baited with urine- and faeces-soiled bedding of male mice captured adult female, but not male, mice, indicating dissemination of sex-attractant semiochemicals from the males’ excreta.

pmc-11960729.title: Uncovering the hidden world of riverbed sediments: The role of sediment heterogeneity and cross-bar channel fills in the hydrogeochemical dynamics of the hyporheic zone
pmc-11960729.creator: Jeffery T. McGarr, Pei Li, Robert G. Ford, Teagan Kleman, Colton Fields, Julie Hobbs, Lydia Lupton, Emma Poston, Thomas Marsh, Leah Trutschel, Ken M. Fritz, Annette Rowe, Corey D. Wallace, Dylan Ward, Daniel M. Sturmer, Craig Dietsch, Margaret Naber, Bob K. Lien, Mohamad Reza Soltanian
pmc-11960729.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Groundwater-surface water interaction (hyporheic exchange) is critical in numerous hydrogeochemical processes; however, hyporheic exchange is difficult to characterize due to the various spatial (e.g., sedimentary architecture) and temporal (e.g., stage fluctuations) variables that influence it. This interdisciplinary study brings forth novel insights by integrating various methodologies including geophysical surveys, physical and chemical sediment characterization, and water chemistry analysis to explore the interplay of the numerous facets governing hyporheic zone processes within a compound bar deposit.

pmc-12647139.title: Resonance peak extraction method based on human ear model and its application in bearing fault diagnosis
pmc-12647139.creator: Yongming Zhao, Yungong Li, Chao Wang, Shiyu Yan, Jiazhuang Dong, Jinxin Yang
pmc-12647139.description: Rolling bearings are crucial in rotating machinery, and combining natural and characteristic frequencies improves fault detection. However, natural frequencies face challenges like feature extraction difficulties and drift, necessitating resonance peak information supplementation. Existing methods for extracting resonance peaks often struggle with low quality, false peaks, and merging issues.

pmc-12732954.title: The Disruption of Cyp7b1 Controls IGFBP2 and Prediabetes Exerted Through Different Hydroxycholesterol Metabolites
pmc-12732954.creator: Roberto Martínez-Beamonte, Natalia Guillén, Javier Sánchez-Marco, Luis V Herrera-Marcos, Joaquín C Surra, María A Navarro, Cristina Barranquero, Carmen Arnal, Juan J Puente, Ma Jesús Rodríguez-Yoldi, Isabel Mendiara, Celia Domeño, Cristina Nerín, Aron M Geurts, Jesús Osada, Martín Laclaustra, Sigrun
pmc-12732954.description: Cytochrome P450, family 7, subfamily b, polypeptide 1 (CYP7B1) is a widely expressed enzyme involved in the hydroxylation of sterols. Generated by transposon technology in zygotes, male rats lacking Cyp7b1 expression in homozygosis showed an absence of Cyp7b1 mRNA expression in the liver, small intestine, adipose tissue, and muscle.

pmc-12867193.title: Correlation of Sclerostin Serum Levels with the Pathogenesis of Coronary Artery Disease
pmc-12867193.creator: Shahlaa Shafiq Rozoqi, Thikra Ali Allwsh
pmc-12867193.description: Background:Sclerostin is primarily known for its role in inhibiting bone formation; however, emerging evidence suggests that it may also play a role in vascular health. Coronary artery disease (CAD) is a heart condition characterized by the narrowing or blockage of the coronary arteries. The relationship between sclerostin and CAD is complex and not yet fully understood.

pmc-13207497.title: Clinical Utility of Quantitative MRI Parameters for Differentiation of Renal Tumor Subtypes and Who Grades: A Multiparametric Approach with Internal Cortical Reference
pmc-13207497.creator: Ekrem Anil Sari, Serap Sari, Canan Altay, Altug Didikoglu, Furkan Mert Kervan, Mustafa Secil
pmc-13207497.description: Background/Objectives: To evaluate the clinical utility and diagnostic performance of quantitative MRI parameters (T1, T2*, R2*, and ADC) in differentiating renal tumor subtypes and WHO grades, and to assess their potential role in non-invasive tumor characterization. Methods: This retrospective study included 82 patients with histopathologically confirmed renal tumors who underwent preoperative contrast-enhanced MRI between July 2019 and January 2024.
